name: Yazid ibn Abi Habib
nameAr: يزيد بن أبي حبيب (واسم أبيه سويد) الأزدي مولاهم، أبو رجاء المصري
mawla: Sharik ibn al-Tufayl al-Azdi, an ally of Banu Malik ibn Hisl of Amir ibn Lu'ayy (al-Mizzi); Ibn Sa'd makes him a mawla of Banu Amir ibn Lu'ayy of Quraysh; the Taqrib says his clientage is disputed
bornNote: 53 (Shamela record); al-Mizzi reports that he lived to over seventy-five, and the Taqrib that he died approaching eighty, which agrees.

taqrib.en: Reliable, a jurist; he would narrate in the disconnected form.

role: Mufti of Egypt in his time (Ibn Yunus)

teachers.name: Abu al-Khayr Marthad ibn Abdullah al-Yazani
teachers.nameAr: أبو الخير مرثد بن عبد الله اليزني

teachers.name: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, by correspondence
teachers.nameAr: محمد بن مسلم بن شهاب الزهري
teachers.source: Tahdhib al-Kamal 32/104 (فيما كتب إليه); Abu Dawud: he did not hear from al-Zuhri

students.name: Amr ibn al-Harith, Muslim's second route

verdicts.ar: يزيد بن أبي حبيب عن عقبة بن عامر مرسل
verdicts.en: Yazid ibn Abi Habib's narration from Uqbah ibn Amir is disconnected (mursal).

verdicts.ar: كان ثقة كثير الحديث، مات سنة ثمان وعشرين ومائة
verdicts.en: He was reliable and prolific; he died in 128.

verdicts.ar: يزيد بن أبي حبيب سيدنا وعالمنا
verdicts.en: Yazid ibn Abi Habib is our master and our scholar.

verdicts.ar: كان مفتي أهل مصر في أيامه، وكان حليما عاقلا، وكان أول من أظهر العلم بمصر والكلام في الحلال والحرام ومسائل، وقيل إنهم كانوا قبل ذلك يتحدثون بالفتن والملاحم والترغيب في الخير
verdicts.en: He was the mufti of Egypt in his day, forbearing and intelligent, and the first to make learning public in Egypt and to speak of the lawful and unlawful and of legal questions; before that, it is said, they spoke of tribulations, apocalyptic battles and exhortation.
verdicts.source: Tahdhib al-Kamal 32/102; Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 4/408; quoted by al-Nawawi, Sharh Muslim 2/11

verdicts.en: He did not hear from al-Zuhri.
Reliable, a jurist; he would narrate in the disconnected form.

dhahabi.ar: وكان حبشيا ثقة، من العلماء الحكماء الأتقياء
dhahabi.en: He was Abyssinian, reliable, one of the learned, the wise and the God-fearing.

notHeardFrom.name: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri
notHeardFrom.counter: Al-Mizzi lists al-Zuhri among his teachers with the gloss "by correspondence" (فيما كتب إليه), so the link is epistolary rather than heard.

notHeardFrom.name: Ibn Umar and any Companion
notHeardFrom.source: al-Daraqutni, al-Ilal 4/98, as cited in the editor's note to Tahdhib al-Kamal 32/106

flags.label: Irsal
flags.detail: The Taqrib's "he would narrate in the disconnected form" rests on Abu Hatim (from Uqbah ibn Amir), Abu Dawud (from al-Zuhri), Ibn Bukayr (from Ibn Shihab and Nafi') and al-Daraqutni (from Ibn Umar and every Companion). In hadith 12 his shaykh is Abu al-Khayr, a fellow Egyptian Successor from whom his hearing is not questioned.

flags.label: Disputed clientage
flags.detail: Al-Mizzi: a mawla of Sharik ibn al-Tufayl al-Azdi; or his father was a mawla of a woman of Banu Hisl and his mother a mawlah of Tujib; Ibn Sa'd: a mawla of Banu Amir ibn Lu'ayy. The Taqrib simply records the disagreement.

bio: The man who, in Ibn Yunus's account, turned Egyptian learning from stories of tribulations and battles to the law of the lawful and the unlawful, and was the mufti of Egypt in his day; al-Layth, his student, called him "our master and our scholar", and al-Dhahabi notes he was Abyssinian. His own teacher Abu al-Khayr had held the fatwa of Egypt before him and al-Layth after him, which is the succession of three muftis in one chain. The critics' only reservation is irsal: he narrated from Companions and from al-Zuhri whom he had not heard.

provenance.ref: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 4/408, as collected on the Shamela narrator record 7035
